Setting up the logbook simulator: a user guide

Henning Winker
FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Division, Assessment and Management Team (NFIFM)
henning.winker@fao.org

simulate_logbook() generates the kind of logbook an analyst receives from a mixed demersal-pelagic fishery, together with the truth that is never in a real logbook: where and with which tactic each trip fished, which vessel type made it, and how the stocks really changed. This guide walks through the simulator layer by layer, explains the settings that matter for targeting, and shows the basic mechanics: what the principal components (PCs) and clusters of the catch composition pick up when we know the truth.

The standardisation of three species from this logbook is shown in Standardising a realistic logbook: two worked examples.

Layer What it does Main settings
Environment shelf-to-slope depth, reef patches in sediment, SST gradient grid, shelf_depth, reef_share, reef_scale, sst_range
Species demersal: depth x substrate; pelagic: SST, depth and season species (one row per species)
Tactics gear catchability of each species tactics (tactic x species)
Fleet vessel types, home tactics and loyalty, entry and exit vessel_types, home, loyalty, entry_share, exit_share
Behaviour trips go where expected value is high price_periods, preference, closure
Dynamics Schaefer production, movement, monthly removals r, B0, B_start, dispersal
Reporting trip records, two-set trips, coarse positions, rounding, under-reporting, synonyms logbook

1. Settings

All settings are in one list. Change any element and pass the list to simulate_logbook(); species, tactics, price, trips, closure, vessel_types, home and loyalty are replaced as a whole, the others are merged with the defaults.

s <- logbook_settings()
names(s)
##  [1] "n_years"           "start_year"        "grid"              "shelf_depth"      
##  [5] "shelf_power"       "depth_sd"          "depth_scale"       "reef_share"       
##  [9] "reef_scale"        "sst_range"         "sst_sd"            "sst_scale"        
## [13] "species"           "tactics"           "q"                 "price_periods"    
## [17] "price"             "vessel_types"      "home"              "loyalty"          
## [21] "vessel_cv"         "entry_share"       "creep"             "exit_share"       
## [25] "trips"             "trips_cv"          "effort_season_amp" "hours_mean"       
## [29] "hours_cv"          "preference"        "closure"           "tweedie_power"    
## [33] "tweedie_phi"       "logbook"
knitr::kable(s$species[, c("species", "group", "habitat", "depth_mu", "reef",
                           "sediment", "sst_mu", "season_amp", "price")],
             row.names = FALSE)
species group habitat depth_mu reef sediment sst_mu season_amp price
Dentex dentex demersal shallow reef 60 1.00 0.02 NA 0.0 12
Pagellus erythrinus demersal shallow sediment 50 0.05 1.00 NA 0.0 8
Pagellus bogaraveo demersal deep reef 350 1.00 0.02 NA 0.0 15
Merluccius merluccius demersal deep sediment 400 0.05 1.00 NA 0.0 5
Conger conger demersal reef, all depths 150 1.00 0.30 NA 0.0 3
Phycis blennoides demersal deep, mixed 500 0.50 1.00 NA 0.0 2
Thunnus alalunga pelagic offshore 700 1.00 1.00 18 0.7 6
Coryphaena hippurus pelagic warm, offshore 300 1.00 1.00 21 0.9 7
Seriola dumerili pelagic coastal, reef-associated 100 1.00 0.30 20 0.4 9
Scomber colias pelagic coastal 60 1.00 1.00 18 0.3 2 
sim <- simulate_logbook(s, seed = 1)

2. Environment

Depth increases offshore (to the right) with random bumps; reef patches are the highest values of a smooth random field; sea temperature increases from north (top, cool) to south (bottom, warm), as in the Southern Hemisphere.

sim$Plots$env

sim$Plots$sst

Reef patches. reef_share is the share of cells that are reef and reef_scale the size (correlation length, in cells) of the patches.

  • Lower reef_share or reef_scale: fewer or smaller, scattered patches. When patches are smaller than the reporting blocks (logbook$obs_res, 5 x 5 cells), reef and sediment trips share the same reported position, so a spatial term cannot separate them and only the catch composition can.
  • Higher values: larger, connected reef areas that a spatial term on the reported positions can resolve.

The default (reef_scale = 2.5) deliberately makes patches about the size of a reporting block or smaller.

reef_maps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 2.5, 6), function(sc) {
  e <- simulate_logbook(modifyList(s, list(reef_scale = sc, n_years = 4)),
                        seed = 1, plots = FALSE)$env
  data.frame(e, reef_scale = paste("reef_scale =", sc))
}))
ggplot(reef_maps, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = substrate)) +
  geom_raster() + facet_wrap(~reef_scale) + coord_equal() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0.5, 40.5, by = 5), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq(0.5, 40.5, by = 5), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(reef = "#7570b3", sediment = "#e6ab02")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL, subtitle = "white grid: 5 x 5 reporting blocks") +
  theme_bw()

3. Species and habitats

Demersal densities are the product of a depth preference (lognormal, depth_mu, depth_cv) and a substrate affinity (reef, sediment), so shallow reef, deep reef, shallow sediment and deep sediment arise as continuous gradients rather than sharp classes. Pelagic species follow sea temperature (sst_mu, sst_sd) and depth, and their availability changes over the year (season_amp, season_peak): dolphinfish and albacore are summer-autumn migrants.

sim$Plots$density

4. Tactics

A tactic is a gear used in a particular way. Its catchability of each species (tactics) is the gear selectivity; where the gear is used decides which species are available. The reef handline catches reef species, the bottom longline sediment species, and pelagic trolling the pelagic species, with some overlap (conger is caught by both bottom gears; amberjack by reef handline and trolling).

q <- as.data.frame(as.table(s$tactics))
names(q) <- c("tactic", "species", "catchability")
ggplot(q, aes(x = species, y = tactic, fill = catchability)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = catchability), size = 2.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 7))

5. Fleet: specialists, mixed vessels and loyalty

Three vessel types (vessel_types) fish with different flexibility:

  • demersal specialists: home tactics reef and sediment;
  • pelagic specialists: home tactic pelagic;
  • mixed vessels: no home preference.

Each month, a share loyalty of a specialist’s trips (default 0.8) is restricted to its home tactics; the remaining trips, and all trips of mixed vessels, choose among all tactics by expected value. Specialists therefore mostly stick to their gear but follow good opportunities, e.g. demersal boats trolling for dolphinfish in a good summer.

s$home
## $demersal
## [1] "Reef"     "Sediment"
## 
## $pelagic
## [1] "Pelagic"
## 
## $mixed
## [1] "Reef"     "Sediment" "Pelagic"
s$loyalty
## demersal  pelagic    mixed 
##      0.8      0.8      0.0
tr <- sim$trips
round(prop.table(table(type = tr$vessel_type, tactic = tr$tactic), 1), 2)
##           tactic
## type       Pelagic Reef Sediment
##   demersal    0.09 0.51     0.41
##   mixed       0.47 0.30     0.23
##   pelagic     0.89 0.06     0.05
tapply(tr$loyal, tr$vessel_type, mean)
##  demersal     mixed   pelagic 
## 0.7966311 0.0000000 0.8069538

Why it matters for standardisation: a specialist’s targeting barely changes, so a vessel effect absorbs it. Mixed vessels (and the non-loyal trips of specialists) switch tactics within the same vessel as prices change, which is the targeting that the catch composition has to capture.

  • loyalty = 1: specialists never leave their home tactics.
  • loyalty = 0 for all types: every vessel behaves as a mixed vessel, the strongest targeting shifts.
  • preference: how strongly trips concentrate on the most valuable cells and tactics (higher = more decisive skippers).

6. Prices, closure and fleet changes

Prices change in three periods: demersal species are expensive in 2000-2007, pelagic species boom in 2008-2015, then prices are neutral. From 2016 the bottom longline is banned deeper than 300 m and effort is cut by 20%. Some vessels enter later (and are more efficient, creep), others leave.

sim$Plots$prices

sim$Plots$tactics

sim$Plots$effort

The result is that nominal CPUE (orange) departs from the true biomass (black) in different ways for each species:

sim$Plots$cpue

7. Reporting: from sets to a logbook

The logbook records trips, not sets. A share logbook$two_sets of trips (default 0.3) makes a second set, and with probability logbook$switch_tactic (default 0.7) the second set uses another tactic. The catches of both sets are summed into one record at the position of the first set, so these trips mix two catch compositions, as in many real logbooks.

mixed <- !is.na(tr$tactic2) & tr$tactic2 != tr$tactic
mean(mixed)                                  # share of trips that mix tactics
## [1] 0.1783129
round(tapply(mixed, tr$vessel_type, mean), 3)
## demersal    mixed  pelagic 
##    0.216    0.207    0.038

Pelagic specialists make mixed trips only on their non-loyal trips. Further reporting settings:

Setting Default Effect
obs_res 5 positions reported as centres of 5 x 5 blocks
missing_position 0.02 share of trips without position
round_to 0.5 catches rounded to 0.5 kg
underreport small catches (< 2 kg) of cheap species (price <= 3) dropped with probability 0.5
synonyms, synonym_rate blackspot seabream 10% recorded under its common name 
head(sim$logbook, 8)

## 2    1 2000     1    V04   7.3 3.85 36.85        Scomber colias  23.5
## 3    1 2000     1    V04   7.3 3.85 36.85      Seriola dumerili  14.0
## 4    2 2000     1    V12   9.7 3.85 36.85         Conger conger  83.5
## 5    2 2000     1    V12   9.7 3.85 36.85 Merluccius merluccius  24.5
## 6    2 2000     1    V12   9.7 3.85 36.85        Scomber colias   3.5
## 7    2 2000     1    V12   9.7 3.85 36.85      Seriola dumerili   9.5

8. Basic mechanics: what the PCs and clusters capture

We now take the logbook through the first steps of the toolbox and compare the targeting covariates with the truth.

x <- cpue_data(sim$logbook, year = "year", species = "species", catch = "kg",
               effort = "hours", id = "trip", vessel = "vessel",
               lon = "lon", lat = "lat", covariates = "month",
               synonyms = c("Blackspot seabream" = "Pagellus bogaraveo"))
x <- subset(x, !is.na(lon), note = "positions reported")
x <- select_species(x, threshold = 0.95)
x <- add_targeting(x)
x$targeting$pca
## <cpue_pca> 19218 operations, 10 species, transform: fourth_root 
##  PC eigenvalue share cumulative
##   1      2.192 0.219      0.219
##   2      1.707 0.171      0.390
##   3      1.340 0.134      0.524
##   4      1.108 0.111      0.635
##   5      1.056 0.106      0.740
##   6      0.792 0.079      0.820
##   7      0.569 0.057      0.876
##   8      0.530 0.053      0.929
## Optimal Coordinates: 3 non-trivial PC(s); 4 clusters by the npc + 1 rule

Attach the truth of each trip (never available in real data):

truth <- sim$trips[match(x$data$trip, sim$trips$trip), ]
x$data$true_tactic <- truth$tactic
x$data$habitat <- ifelse(truth$tactic == "Pelagic", "pelagic", truth$habitat)
x$data$depth <- truth$depth
x$data$mixed <- ifelse(!is.na(truth$tactic2) & truth$tactic2 != truth$tactic,
                       "two tactics", "one tactic")
x$data$X <- truth$X
x$data$Y <- truth$Y

PCs against tactic and habitat

plot_biplot(x, colour_by = "true_tactic")

plot_biplot(x, pcs = c(2, 3), colour_by = "habitat")

Read the axes from the species arrows (loadings). In this fishery the first PC typically separates pelagic from demersal trips, and the next PCs reef from sediment and shallow from deep: the PCA recovers tactic and habitat from the catch alone, without being told either. Which PC carries which contrast can change between runs and settings, so always check the loadings.

PCs against depth and the true position

demersal_trips <- x$data$true_tactic != "Pelagic"
ggplot(x$data[demersal_trips, ], aes(x = depth, y = PC2, colour = true_tactic)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.7) + scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Depth of the first set (m, log scale)", colour = "True tactic",
       title = "Demersal trips: PC2 against depth") + theme_bw()

If depth is carried by another PC in your run, replace PC2 by that PC.

Averaged by the true cell, the PC scores map the habitat at a finer scale than the reported positions; the reported 5 x 5 blocks blur it.

cell_pc <- aggregate(cbind(PC1, PC2) ~ X + Y, data = x$data, FUN = mean)
pm <- rbind(data.frame(X = cell_pc$X, Y = cell_pc$Y, score = cell_pc$PC1, pc = "PC1"),
            data.frame(X = cell_pc$X, Y = cell_pc$Y, score = cell_pc$PC2, pc = "PC2"))
ggplot(pm, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = score)) +
  geom_raster() + facet_wrap(~pc) + coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "grey95", high = "#b2182b") +
  labs(x = "x (offshore ->)", y = "y", fill = "Mean score",
       title = "Mean PC score by true cell") + theme_bw()

plot_targeting(x, res = 0.5)$map_pc

Mixed trips lie between the clusters

plot_biplot(x, colour_by = "mixed")

Trips that combine two tactics have intermediate compositions. PCs place them continuously; clusters have to assign each to one tactic.

Clusters against the true tactic

tactic_table(x)

## cluster deep reef deep sediment pelagic shallow reef shallow sediment
##       1      0.04          0.01    0.43         0.22             0.30
##       2      0.01          0.01    0.96         0.01             0.01
##       3      0.83          0.03    0.05         0.03             0.06
##       4      0.10          0.75    0.07         0.04             0.04

Clusters describe the catch composition, which reflects both the gear and where it was used, so they rarely match tactics one to one: mixed trips, gear overlap and neighbouring habitats blur the link.

Targeting over time

pt <- plot_targeting(x, res = 0.5)
pt$time

pt$pcs_time

sim$Plots$tactics

The clusters and PCs change in steps at the price changes (2008, 2016) and the closure (2016), as the true tactic shares do.

Vessel profiles against the true vessel type

groups <- split(sim$settings$species$species, sim$settings$species$group)
type <- tapply(sim$trips$vessel_type, sprintf("V%02d", sim$trips$vessel),
               function(z) z[1])
plot_vessel_profile(x, groups = groups, by = type)

Specialists sit at the ends (almost all demersal or almost all pelagic catch), mixed vessels in between. With loyalty 0.8 the specialists are clear but not pure, so rules on the catch of the target species (select_vessels()) recover them only approximately.

Things to try

  • Reef patches: reef_scale = 1 against 6, and compare Base+S with DPC+S in the standardisation: the gap shrinks as patches grow larger than the reporting blocks.
  • Loyalty: loyalty = c(demersal = 1, pelagic = 1, mixed = 0) (strict specialists) or all zero (every vessel mixed).
  • Mixed trips: logbook = list(two_sets = 0) (one set per trip) or switch_tactic = 1; see how the clusters separate and how the PC biplot changes.
  • Reporting: obs_res = 1 (exact positions) against 10 (very coarse).
  • Stock trends: change B_start or r so that species trends diverge, and check whether the PCs start absorbing them (compare n_pc).
